+-- Exam & Architectural Insight ------------------------------------------
| Objective: SY0-701 5.6 Security awareness practices: phishing campaigns,
| anomalous behaviour, training, reporting.
| 
| Key Concepts
|   • Phishing campaigns (simulations) measure click, credential-submission
| and report rates; the report rate matters most.
|   • Anomalous behaviour is risky (deliberate rule-bending), unexpected
| (out of pattern) or unintentional (honest mistake).
|   • Training topics: policy/handbooks, situational awareness, insider
| threat, passwords, removable media and cables, social engineering, OPSEC,
| hybrid/remote work.
|   • Initial training happens at onboarding; recurring training keeps it
| current. Reporting and monitoring track both.
|   • A program is developed (goals, audience, content), executed (delivery,
| simulations) and measured against KPIs.
| 
| Manual Failure Modes
|   • Punishing every click: people stop reporting, and the report rate is
| your early-warning sensor.
|   • One annual video and no simulations: no data on who actually
| recognises a phish.
|   • Same thresholds for the finance clerk and the payroll admin, although
| BEC targets high-risk roles.
|   • Treating a missing training record as 'probably done' instead of
| untrained.
|   • Sending insider-threat suspicions to the user's manager first, so
| evidence disappears.
| 
| How to Govern an AI Agent Here
|   • An AI mail triage agent should score indicators and explain each one,
| not just say 'safe'.
|   • Message bodies are untrusted input: the agent must never follow
| instructions found inside an email.
|   • An agent may assign micro-training automatically, but escalation and
| insider-threat referral need a human.
|   • Log every classification with the policy version so behaviour verdicts
| can be audited and contested.
| 
| Exam Tips
|   • Suspected phish: report it (Report Phishing button / SOC), do not
| click, reply or forward it to colleagues.
|   • Lookalike domain (examp1e.com) = typosquatting; wire-transfer request
| from a 'CEO' = BEC / impersonation.
|   • 'Employee plugs in a USB drive found in the car park' = removable
| media training (baiting).
|   • Risky = intentional, unexpected = deviates from baseline,
| unintentional = accident: know the three words.
|   • Initial vs recurring is about training cadence; computer-based
| training (CBT) and gamification are delivery methods.

+-- Exam & Architectural Insight ------------------------------------------
| Objective: SY0-701 5.6 Security awareness practices: phishing campaigns,
| anomalous behaviour, training, reporting.
| 
| Key Concepts
|   • Phishing campaigns (simulations) measure click, credential-submission
| and report rates; the report rate matters most.
|   • Anomalous behaviour is risky (deliberate rule-bending), unexpected
| (out of pattern) or unintentional (honest mistake).
|   • Training topics: policy/handbooks, situational awareness, insider
| threat, passwords, removable media and cables, social engineering, OPSEC,
| hybrid/remote work.
|   • Initial training happens at onboarding; recurring training keeps it
| current. Reporting and monitoring track both.
|   • A program is developed (goals, audience, content), executed (delivery,
| simulations) and measured against KPIs.
| 
| Manual Failure Modes
|   • Punishing every click: people stop reporting, and the report rate is
| your early-warning sensor.
|   • One annual video and no simulations: no data on who actually
| recognises a phish.
|   • Same thresholds for the finance clerk and the payroll admin, although
| BEC targets high-risk roles.
|   • Treating a missing training record as 'probably done' instead of
| untrained.
|   • Sending insider-threat suspicions to the user's manager first, so
| evidence disappears.
| 
| How to Govern an AI Agent Here
|   • An AI mail triage agent should score indicators and explain each one,
| not just say 'safe'.
|   • Message bodies are untrusted input: the agent must never follow
| instructions found inside an email.
|   • An agent may assign micro-training automatically, but escalation and
| insider-threat referral need a human.
|   • Log every classification with the policy version so behaviour verdicts
| can be audited and contested.
| 
| Exam Tips
|   • Suspected phish: report it (Report Phishing button / SOC), do not
| click, reply or forward it to colleagues.
|   • Lookalike domain (examp1e.com) = typosquatting; wire-transfer request
| from a 'CEO' = BEC / impersonation.
|   • 'Employee plugs in a USB drive found in the car park' = removable
| media training (baiting).
|   • Risky = intentional, unexpected = deviates from baseline,
| unintentional = accident: know the three words.
|   • Initial vs recurring is about training cadence; computer-based
| training (CBT) and gamification are delivery methods.

| Objective: SY0-701 5.6 Security awareness practices: phishing campaigns,
| anomalous behaviour, training, reporting.
| 
| Key Concepts
|   • Phishing campaigns (simulations) measure click, credential-submission
| and report rates; the report rate matters most.
|   • Anomalous behaviour is risky (deliberate rule-bending), unexpected
| (out of pattern) or unintentional (honest mistake).
|   • Training topics: policy/handbooks, situational awareness, insider
| threat, passwords, removable media and cables, social engineering, OPSEC,
| hybrid/remote work.
|   • Initial training happens at onboarding; recurring training keeps it
| current. Reporting and monitoring track both.
|   • A program is developed (goals, audience, content), executed (delivery,
| simulations) and measured against KPIs.
| 
| Manual Failure Modes
|   • Punishing every click: people stop reporting, and the report rate is
| your early-warning sensor.
|   • One annual video and no simulations: no data on who actually
| recognises a phish.
|   • Same thresholds for the finance clerk and the payroll admin, although
| BEC targets high-risk roles.
|   • Treating a missing training record as 'probably done' instead of
| untrained.
|   • Sending insider-threat suspicions to the user's manager first, so
| evidence disappears.
| 
| How to Govern an AI Agent Here
|   • An AI mail triage agent should score indicators and explain each one,
| not just say 'safe'.
|   • Message bodies are untrusted input: the agent must never follow
| instructions found inside an email.
|   • An agent may assign micro-training automatically, but escalation and
| insider-threat referral need a human.
|   • Log every classification with the policy version so behaviour verdicts
| can be audited and contested.
| 
| Exam Tips
|   • Suspected phish: report it (Report Phishing button / SOC), do not
| click, reply or forward it to colleagues.
|   • Lookalike domain (examp1e.com) = typosquatting; wire-transfer request
| from a 'CEO' = BEC / impersonation.
|   • 'Employee plugs in a USB drive found in the car park' = removable
| media training (baiting).
|   • Risky = intentional, unexpected = deviates from baseline,
| unintentional = accident: know the three words.
|   • Initial vs recurring is about training cadence; computer-based
| training (CBT) and gamification are delivery methods.

+-- Exam & Architectural Insight ------------------------------------------
| Objective: SY0-701 5.6 Security awareness practices: phishing campaigns,
| anomalous behaviour, training, reporting.
| 
| Key Concepts
|   • Phishing campaigns (simulations) measure click, credential-submission
| and report rates; the report rate matters most.
|   • Anomalous behaviour is risky (deliberate rule-bending), unexpected
| (out of pattern) or unintentional (honest mistake).
|   • Training topics: policy/handbooks, situational awareness, insider
| threat, passwords, removable media and cables, social engineering, OPSEC,
| hybrid/remote work.
|   • Initial training happens at onboarding; recurring training keeps it
| current. Reporting and monitoring track both.
|   • A program is developed (goals, audience, content), executed (delivery,
| simulations) and measured against KPIs.
| 
| Manual Failure Modes
|   • Punishing every click: people stop reporting, and the report rate is
| your early-warning sensor.
|   • One annual video and no simulations: no data on who actually
| recognises a phish.
|   • Same thresholds for the finance clerk and the payroll admin, although
| BEC targets high-risk roles.
|   • Treating a missing training record as 'probably done' instead of
| untrained.
|   • Sending insider-threat suspicions to the user's manager first, so
| evidence disappears.
| 
| How to Govern an AI Agent Here
|   • An AI mail triage agent should score indicators and explain each one,
| not just say 'safe'.
|   • Message bodies are untrusted input: the agent must never follow
| instructions found inside an email.
|   • An agent may assign micro-training automatically, but escalation and
| insider-threat referral need a human.
|   • Log every classification with the policy version so behaviour verdicts
| can be audited and contested.
| 
| Exam Tips
|   • Suspected phish: report it (Report Phishing button / SOC), do not
| click, reply or forward it to colleagues.
|   • Lookalike domain (examp1e.com) = typosquatting; wire-transfer request
| from a 'CEO' = BEC / impersonation.
|   • 'Employee plugs in a USB drive found in the car park' = removable
| media training (baiting).
|   • Risky = intentional, unexpected = deviates from baseline,
| unintentional = accident: know the three words.
|   • Initial vs recurring is about training cadence; computer-based
| training (CBT) and gamification are delivery methods.

+-- Exam & Architectural Insight ------------------------------------------
| Objective: SY0-701 5.6 Security awareness practices: phishing campaigns,
| anomalous behaviour, training, reporting.
| 
| Key Concepts
|   • Phishing campaigns (simulations) measure click, credential-submission
| and report rates; the report rate matters most.
|   • Anomalous behaviour is risky (deliberate rule-bending), unexpected
| (out of pattern) or unintentional (honest mistake).
|   • Training topics: policy/handbooks, situational awareness, insider
| threat, passwords, removable media and cables, social engineering, OPSEC,
| hybrid/remote work.
|   • Initial training happens at onboarding; recurring training keeps it
| current. Reporting and monitoring track both.
|   • A program is developed (goals, audience, content), executed (delivery,
| simulations) and measured against KPIs.
| 
| Manual Failure Modes
|   • Punishing every click: people stop reporting, and the report rate is
| your early-warning sensor.
|   • One annual video and no simulations: no data on who actually
| recognises a phish.
|   • Same thresholds for the finance clerk and the payroll admin, although
| BEC targets high-risk roles.
|   • Treating a missing training record as 'probably done' instead of
| untrained.
|   • Sending insider-threat suspicions to the user's manager first, so
| evidence disappears.
| 
| How to Govern an AI Agent Here
|   • An AI mail triage agent should score indicators and explain each one,
| not just say 'safe'.
|   • Message bodies are untrusted input: the agent must never follow
| instructions found inside an email.
|   • An agent may assign micro-training automatically, but escalation and
| insider-threat referral need a human.
|   • Log every classification with the policy version so behaviour verdicts
| can be audited and contested.
| 
| Exam Tips
|   • Suspected phish: report it (Report Phishing button / SOC), do not
| click, reply or forward it to colleagues.
|   • Lookalike domain (examp1e.com) = typosquatting; wire-transfer request
| from a 'CEO' = BEC / impersonation.
|   • 'Employee plugs in a USB drive found in the car park' = removable
| media training (baiting).
|   • Risky = intentional, unexpected = deviates from baseline,
| unintentional = accident: know the three words.
|   • Initial vs recurring is about training cadence; computer-based
| training (CBT) and gamification are delivery methods.

+-- Exam & Architectural Insight ------------------------------------------
| Objective: SY0-701 5.6 Security awareness practices: phishing campaigns,
| anomalous behaviour, training, reporting.
| 
| Key Concepts
|   • Phishing campaigns (simulations) measure click, credential-submission
| and report rates; the report rate matters most.
|   • Anomalous behaviour is risky (deliberate rule-bending), unexpected
| (out of pattern) or unintentional (honest mistake).
|   • Training topics: policy/handbooks, situational awareness, insider
| threat, passwords, removable media and cables, social engineering, OPSEC,
| hybrid/remote work.
|   • Initial training happens at onboarding; recurring training keeps it
| current. Reporting and monitoring track both.
|   • A program is developed (goals, audience, content), executed (delivery,
| simulations) and measured against KPIs.
| 
| Manual Failure Modes
|   • Punishing every click: people stop reporting, and the report rate is
| your early-warning sensor.
|   • One annual video and no simulations: no data on who actually
| recognises a phish.
|   • Same thresholds for the finance clerk and the payroll admin, although
| BEC targets high-risk roles.
|   • Treating a missing training record as 'probably done' instead of
| untrained.
|   • Sending insider-threat suspicions to the user's manager first, so
| evidence disappears.
| 
| How to Govern an AI Agent Here
|   • An AI mail triage agent should score indicators and explain each one,
| not just say 'safe'.
|   • Message bodies are untrusted input: the agent must never follow
| instructions found inside an email.
|   • An agent may assign micro-training automatically, but escalation and
| insider-threat referral need a human.
|   • Log every classification with the policy version so behaviour verdicts
| can be audited and contested.
| 
| Exam Tips
|   • Suspected phish: report it (Report Phishing button / SOC), do not
| click, reply or forward it to colleagues.
|   • Lookalike domain (examp1e.com) = typosquatting; wire-transfer request
| from a 'CEO' = BEC / impersonation.
|   • 'Employee plugs in a USB drive found in the car park' = removable
| media training (baiting).
|   • Risky = intentional, unexpected = deviates from baseline,
| unintentional = accident: know the three words.
|   • Initial vs recurring is about training cadence; computer-based
| training (CBT) and gamification are delivery methods.
